S038-01.notes: The colon explains the blank: the committee can review and recommend, but it cannot approve, reject or delay spending. That describes limited authority, so 'circumscribed' fits. 'Absolute' says the opposite. 'Redundant' and 'unprecedented' have no support in the text. I inserted all four words into the sentence and only B works.

S038-02.notes: The seafloor-spreading evidence supplied the mechanism Wegener lacked, so his claim was 'vindicated'. 'Undermined' reverses the meaning. 'Anticipated' does not fit 'by evidence'. The facts check out: Wegener proposed drift in 1912, died in 1930, and seafloor spreading was mapped around 1960, roughly half a century later.

S038-03.notes: The last sentence says the Cavendish now dominates 'in the same way' and that a new strain of the same fungus is attacking it, so the old vulnerability is repeating. B is wrong because the earlier text already says why growers switched. C and D are not supported. The facts are accurate: Gros Michel, Panama disease, the switch to Cavendish, and the new strain (TR4).

S038-04.notes: The text links the switch to swarming with a rise in serotonin. If a drug blocks serotonin's effects, the switch should largely fail. This matches Anstey et al. (2009). A and B reverse the logic. D goes beyond the text, which says nothing about touch on other body parts.

flags: minor: the key is the longest choice, but it has to be, because only it covers all three conditions the claim needs (red, darkness, white)
S038-05.notes: The claim needs light-avoiding bats under red light (36) to be close to darkness (40), and white light (10) to be much lower. Only D gives all three numbers. A uses only light-tolerant bats. B leaves out the red and white conditions. C compares the wrong groups.

S038-06.notes: Text 2 says environment and habits are a confound: sense of direction tracked environment about as closely as it tracked language. So the critics would say language alone may not explain it. C is wrong because the critics do not dispute the speakers' accuracy. D contradicts Text 2. A is the opposite of their view.

S038-07.notes: A is the only choice that contrasts the light each telescope observes. D mentions Webb only. B is about launch dates and C is about orbit distance. The facts match the notes.

S038-08.notes: The sentence admits a drawback, and the next sentence answers it with 'however'. That concede-then-counter pattern calls for 'Granted'. 'Consequently' and 'Likewise' need an earlier sentence, and the blank opens the passage. 'Specifically' has nothing to make more specific.

S038-09.notes: The clause after the colon is a direct question ('where do European eels go to spawn'), so it needs a question mark. The fact checks out: Johannes Schmidt traced the larvae to the Sargasso Sea in the 1920s.

S038-10.notes: This is a past counterfactual: the main clause uses 'would probably have broken' and the event is the 2020 pass, so the if-clause needs the past perfect 'had passed'. The other three tenses do not fit.
